name: nav-path-following-visual
description: Tests path following and stuck state with building obstacles

steps.description: A third driller so the three offices go up one apiece (#556). Ordering a building is queued work now, and two drillers splitting three builds spend long enough on them to cross their own collapse threshold — a collapsing employee never attempts a path, so the stuck state this file exists to watch would never be reached.

First wall segment: seals the east side of the (0,0) corner (x:2-3, z:0-1). #556: confirming a placement only queues a construction site now — one of the two idle drillers hired above walks over and builds each wall segment for real; a waitUntil step below drives all three to completion before employee #1 is dispatched toward the now-sealed corner.
Second wall segment: seals the south side of the (0,0) corner (x:0-1, z:2-3).
Third wall segment: fills the diagonal corner gap (x:2-3, z:2-3) so no 8-directional diagonal move can slip past the wall.

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556) — the next step waits for all three wall segments to actually land before the corner is genuinely sealed.

steps.description: Drive all three wall-segment sites to completion (#556) — one of the two idle drillers does the walking/building.

#556: dispatched only now that the corner is already fully sealed (previously dispatched before the walls existed, mid-walk — construction is no longer instant, so a wall built out from under an already-close walker no longer happens; dispatching into an already-sealed target every re-route attempt fails immediately instead). Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one... which left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`. Employee 3, the fresh hire above, rather than employee 1 (#556): the builders are collapsing by this point and would never attempt the path. Dispatched OUT of the walled-off corner rather than into it (#556). The three offices seal the (0,0)–(1,1) pocket either way; what changed is which side of the wall the crew is on. Ordering a building is queued work now, so the drillers walk to the sites and are relocated off each finished footprint onto the nearest walkable tile — which is inside the pocket they have just closed. An unreachable goal is an unreachable goal in either direction, and this is still exactly the state the file watches: stuckEmployeeCount 1 while the wall stands, 0 once the demolitions below reopen it.
Every re-route attempt now fails since (0,0) is fully enclosed — after STUCK_THRESHOLD consecutive failures employee #1 flips to the stuck state.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

Re-dispatched to the same unreachable target (#556). The crew builds the offices now instead of them appearing on confirm, so by this point Walt’s own need drain has him claiming a rest and dropping the impossible walk — the state this file measures is the walled-off route, so it is re-issued rather than allowed to lapse.

expect.note: Shortened 10 -> 5 ticks (#556): the crew now spends ~65 ticks building the three offices before this block, so Walt enters it with fatigue already at ~35 and collapses 13 ticks in — and a collapsed employee is not a stuck one. Ten more ticks would have measured the collapse rather than the walled-off route this file is about; five keeps the whole block inside the window where the route itself is what is failing.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.
Demolish all three wall segments — the previously stuck agent should be able to resume movement once the corner is fully open again.
Advance ticks after demolition — the stuck agent should resume moving toward its destination.
